slo_title: Define convolution of two functions and state the convolution theorem

mcq.q: \(\text{If } F\{f(t)\} = F(s) \text{ and } F\{g(t)\} = G(s), \text{ then according to the convolution theorem:}\)
\(\text{The convolution of two functions } f(t) \text{ and } g(t) \text{ in the context of Fourier transforms is defined as:}\)

\(\text{Given } f(t) = \begin{cases} 1, & 0 \leq t \leq 3 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \text{ and } g(t) = \begin{cases} 1, & 0 \leq t \leq 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}, \text{ what is } (f*g)(t) \text{ for } 2 \leq t < 3?\)
\(\text{For two rectangular pulses of equal width } a, \text{ the convolution results in a:}\)
\(\text{The inverse Fourier transform of the product } F(s)G(s) \text{ is:}\)

sq.q: \(\text{Define convolution of two functions. State and prove the convolution theorem for Fourier transforms.}\)
answer: \(= \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t) g(x-t) e^{i s x} dt dx\)
\(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t) e^{i s t} dt \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} g(u) e^{i s u} du = F(s) G(s)\)

sq.q: \(\text{Use convolution theorem to find the inverse Fourier transform of } \frac{1}{(1+is)(2+is)}.\)
answer: \(\text{We know } f(x) = e^{-x} u(x), g(x) = e^{-2x} u(x) \text{ where } u(x) \text{ is unit step}\)
\(\text{By convolution theorem, inverse of } F(s)G(s) \text{ is } (f*g)(x)\)
\((f*g)(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t) g(x-t) dt = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{0}^{x} e^{-t} e^{-2(x-t)} dt \text{ for } x>0\)
\(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} (e^{-x} - e^{-2x}) \text{ for } x>0, \text{ and 0 for } x<0.\)

lq.q: \(\text{Using convolution theorem, find the inverse Fourier transform of } \frac{1}{(a+is)(b+is)}.\)
answer: Step Marks Let \(F(s) = \frac{1}{a+is} \cdot \frac{1}{b+is}\) (1) We know: \(\mathcal{F}\{e^{-ax}u(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{a+is}\) where \(u(x)\) is unit step (3) Similarly: \(\mathcal{F}\{e^{-bx}u(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{b+is}\) (3) By convolution theorem: \(\mathcal{F}^{-1}\{F(s)\} = \sqrt{2\pi} [e^{-ax}u(x) * e^{-bx}u(x)]\) (2) Compute convolution: \((e^{-ax}u(x) * e^{-bx}u(x)) = \int_{0}^{x} e^{-at} e^{-b(x-t)} dt\) for \(x > 0\) (3) \(= e^{-bx} \int_{0}^{x} e^{(b-a)t} dt = e^{-bx} \left[ \frac{e^{(b-a)t}}{b-a} \right]_{0}^{x}\) (3) \(= \frac{e^{-ax} - e^{-bx}}{b-a}\) for \(x > 0\), and \(0\) for \(x < 0\) (3)
